issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares numberOfInscribedStudents as an int, but the solution implementation declares numberOfInscribedStudents as a long. This attribute type mismatch is structural and will confuse students about the expected type and can lead to compilation issues or failing tests that expect int.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute types consistent. Change numberOfInscribedStudents in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java from long to int, and update the constructor parameter, getter, setter, and any usages (toString, calculations) accordingly so they match the UML and expected tests. Alternatively, if large values are intended, update the problem statement/UML and tests to use long for this attribute and related methods.

issues.description: getTotalNumberOfStudents() is specified in the UML to return an int, and the solution's method signature declares an int return type, but because numberOfInscribedStudents is implemented as a long the expression numberOfGuestStudents + numberOfInscribedStudents is of type long. Returning this long expression from a method declared to return int causes a compilation/type mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure returned expression type matches the method signature. Preferably change numberOfInscribedStudents to int (see previous fix) so the addition yields an int and the current int return type is correct. Alternatively, if numberOfInscribedStudents must remain long, change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return long and update the UML/problem statement and any dependent methods/tests accordingly.
